problem: The step says 'Freeze every convolution and pooling layer'. Batch-normalization layers are neither convolution nor pooling, so a student following this literally would leave the BN parameters trainable. Section 2 later says BN must be handled carefully, so the two parts do not join up.
fix: Say: 'Freeze all parameters of the base (convolution, batch-norm and the old head is removed). Put every batch-norm layer in evaluation mode so it uses stored running mean and variance.'

problem: The step 'Add global pooling and a new K-way fully connected layer' suggests a pooling layer is being added. ResNet-50 already ends with global average pooling before its fully connected layer, so the usual move is to keep the existing pooling and replace only the FC layer.
fix: Say: 'Keep the existing global average pooling; remove the old fully connected layer and add a new K-way fully connected layer.'

problem: The table gives 1e-3 for the new head, while the text says fine-tuning uses a rate 'often 10 to 100 times smaller than training from scratch'. The two statements look contradictory unless the reader knows the small-rate rule applies only to unfrozen pretrained layers, not to the brand-new head.
fix: Add a note under the table: 'The 10x to 100x smaller rule applies to unfrozen pretrained layers. The new head is trained from scratch, so it can use a normal rate near 1e-3.'

problem: Terms central to the numbers are used without definition: 'global average pooling' (never explained as averaging each feature map to one number), 'ResNet-50' and 'residual block' (step 6). A reader on a phone who has not met ResNet cannot picture what is frozen.
fix: Add one line each: global average pooling takes the mean of each feature map, giving one number per channel (2,048 numbers for ResNet-50); a ResNet-50 block is a group of convolution layers with a skip connection; ResNet-50 is a 50-layer convolutional network.

problem: The same number is written two ways: '2048 features' in the figure note and '2,048' in the text. Small, but inconsistent number formatting in a unit book is distracting.
fix: Use '2,048 features' in the figure note as well.

problem: The answer '1e-4 to 1e-5' is right for the unfrozen last block, but a student may carry it over to the new head, which still needs a normal rate near 1e-3.
fix: Add to the answer: 'The new head can still use about 1e-3; only the unfrozen pretrained block uses the small rate.'
